First, we rewrite the limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{5}^{-x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{({5}^{-1})}^{x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943873/assets/0f9cf17608e32b91f4efbb243702286b484938c015f74f0b59ca906dc24c593a.png)

From the graph, we see that the function increases without bound as $x$ decreases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}=\infty .
$$
